name: Concrete Block Calculator
description: Estimate CMU concrete blocks, mortar, core-fill grout, and waste allowance for block walls and foundations.
search_intent: Calculate how many cinder blocks or CMU blocks are needed for a wall.

inputs.label: Block width (nominal 16-inch length × 8-inch height)
inputs.help: Standard 8-in thick, 6-in thick, 4-in partition, or 12-in retaining wall CMU

inputs.label: Core grouting schedule
inputs.help: None (hollow), cores at 32 inches, cores at 16 inches, or 100% solid filled

outputs.label: Whole CMU blocks to order (with waste)

calculation: Gross wall area = length × height. Net area = max(0, gross area − openings). Standard 8x8x16 block has a nominal face dimension of 16 in × 8 in = 128 in² (0.8889 ft²). Face area block factor = 1.125 blocks per square foot of wall face. Exact blocks = net area × 1.125. Purchase blocks = ceil(exact blocks × (1 + waste/100)). Mortar required = approx 13.5 ft³ per 100 blocks at 3/8-inch joint. Core fill grout volume depends on block core volume (approx 0.33 ft³ per 8-in core cell, 2 cores per block) multiplied by grout frequency (none: 0, 32-in: 1 core per 2 blocks, 16-in: 1 core per block, solid: 2 cores per block). Core fill volume is converted to cubic yards (ft³ / 27).
limitations: Grouting requirements, rebar cell placement, and bond beams must be specified by a licensed structural engineer.
Corner blocks, jamb blocks, and lintel bond-beam blocks require separate takeoff for complex wall openings.
Mortar and grout yield vary by mix consistency, moisture absorption, and tooling loss.
